questions.text: What do you do when you feel anxious?

options.text: I tune into my body — where exactly I feel tension or heaviness.
I analyze what's causing the anxiety — what thoughts are running through my mind.
I try to understand where this feeling came from — maybe from childhood.
I ask myself: "What is this anxiety telling me about my values?"
I switch to activities — a walk, chores, talking to a friend.
I pray and trust God — it brings back peace.
I remind myself that everything is from the Almighty, and ease follows hardship.

questions.text: How do you handle conflict with someone close?

options.text: I express what I'm feeling right now, without blame.
I look for concrete agreements and steps to resolve it.
I try to understand what's really going on beneath the words.
I reflect on forgiveness and what matters more — being right or keeping peace.
I think about freedom and responsibility each of us has.
I take a pause, let emotions cool down — then talk.
I trust that time and good deeds will ease the tension.

questions.text: How do you make important decisions?

options.text: I listen to my inner compass — what feels right on a sensory level.
I weigh pros and cons, make a list of arguments.
I look for signs, answers in sacred texts or prayer.
I consult those I trust and seek wisdom in community.
I reflect on the finiteness of life and what truly matters.
I trust the flow of life — if the decision is right, things will fall into place.
I explore my past decision-making patterns.

questions.text: What helps you in difficult times?

options.text: Body practices — breathing, movement, grounding.
A concrete action plan for the coming days.
A sense that this trial has meaning, even if I can't see it yet.
Hope and trust that everything is in the hands of a higher power.
Understanding that suffering is part of the human experience.
Trust that things will work out — I live one day at a time.
Analyzing which childhood patterns are being triggered.

questions.text: How do you take care of yourself?

options.text: I listen to my body — sleep, food, movement, rest when needed.
I plan my routine and stick to it — structure helps.
I explore my feelings and needs through journaling or therapy.
I make time for what truly matters, not just what's urgent.
I do what I enjoy — books, walks, meeting friends.
Prayer, fasting, reading Scripture — spiritual practice.
Dua, dhikr, reading Quran — that's my source of energy.

questions.text: What do you do when you're angry?

options.text: I pause and feel where the anger lives in my body.
I capture the thought of injustice and look for arguments.
I try to understand what's behind the anger — hurt, fear, exhaustion.
I ask myself: "What am I agreeing to that I don't want?"
I let it go — I rarely get angry, it passes on its own.
I try to understand if I crossed someone's boundary.
I endure and reflect — when to hold back and when to speak.

questions.text: How do you relate to criticism?

options.text: I first feel it in my body — stomach tightens, I tense up. Then I figure it out.
I analyze: is the criticism fair? Are there facts?
I'm curious: what does this say about me? What pattern is visible?
I wonder: maybe this is pointing to something important?
I take note but don't dwell on it — I know my worth.
I reflect: maybe this is a lesson in humility?
I listen to wise people, but the decision is mine.

questions.text: What do you do when you feel stuck?

options.text: I pay attention to what feelings and bodily sensations accompany this state.
I break the big problem into small steps and start with the simplest one.
I look for possible unconscious benefits of staying in this spot.
I ask myself what meaning this stuckness might hold for my path.
I relax and don't pressure myself — sometimes it's better to let go.
I trust that my time hasn't come yet — everything has its season.
I pray or reflect — sometimes answers come not from the mind, but from silence.

questions.text: How do you build relationships with those close to you?

options.text: I try to stay in contact with myself and express what I feel.
I discuss expectations and boundaries — so it's clear for both.
I notice repeating patterns and try to understand them.
I value depth and honesty, even if it hurts.
I give people space and don't try to control.
I build on shared values and mutual respect.
I try to be just and patient.

questions.text: What does "being okay" mean to you?

options.text: Being in contact with my body and feelings — not shutting down.
Having clear goals and moving toward them step by step.
Understanding myself and my motives, even when it's hard.
Accepting uncertainty and finding meaning in it.
Just living — without extra questions and pressure.
Being at peace with God and with myself.
Feeling gratitude and trust in the plan.

questions.text: How do you listen to your body?

options.text: I regularly scan — what hurts, where's the tension, what's needed.
I monitor my routine — sleep, food, exercise. Body as a system.
I notice how emotions manifest in the body — and explore it.
The body is part of my existence, not just a machine.
When I'm tired — I rest. I don't overcomplicate.
The body is a temple of the soul, I care for it as a gift.
Health is an amanah, I try to preserve it.

questions.text: How do you relate to your past?

options.text: I return to bodily sensations — what I felt back then.
I extract lessons — what worked, what didn't.
I explore repeating patterns and their roots.
The past is part of my story, but not a sentence.
I don't look back — I live in the present.
I forgive myself and others — it sets free.
I accept it as part of the path that was destined for me.

questions.text: How do you look at the future?

options.text: I feel it in my body — anxiety or calm say a lot.
I plan and prepare — it gives a sense of control.
I'm curious: what unconscious scripts am I carrying into the future?
The future isn't guaranteed — and that's okay.
Whatever happens — happens. I don't worry in advance.
I trust God — He knows what's best.
I plan, but the outcome is in the hands of the Almighty.
I sit with this feeling — what it does to my body, where it lives.
I look for activities and people — loneliness is solved by action.
I'm curious: where does this come from? Maybe from childhood?
Loneliness is part of the human condition — it doesn't need to be "fixed".
I enjoy solitude — it's time for myself.
In prayer I am never alone.
I trust that the Almighty is always near.

questions.text: What gives you stability in life?

options.text: Contact with my body and breath — an anchor in the moment.
Structure, habits, plan — that's the foundation.
Self-understanding — the better I know myself, the more stable I am.
Freedom to choose my own path, even if it's unpredictable.
Close people and simple joys.
Faith, family, community — something bigger than me.
Faith in the justice and mercy of the Almighty.

C.title: THE STRATEGIST
C.description: You think clearly and step by step. For you, problems are tasks with solutions, and you know how to tackle them. Plans and algorithms are your element.

P.title: SHADOW ARCHAEOLOGIST
P.description: You seek depth and cause. You're curious about where things come from, and you're willing to dig into the past to understand the present. Unconscious scripts aren't an abstraction to you — they're a field for exploration.

G.title: THE FEELING BLADE
G.description: You trust your body and the moment. You care about what's happening right now, and you know how to listen to your sensations. Pausing and feeling is your greatest resource.

E.title: WANDERER WITHOUT A MAP
E.description: You ask the big questions. Meaning, freedom, solitude — these aren't abstractions to you, they're what you deal with every day. You're not looking for ready-made answers — you're looking for your own path.

S.title: THE SELF-GUIDED WAYFARER
S.description: You already have your own resources and ways of coping. Perhaps books, practices, or support from loved ones are enough. You're already moving along your own path.

X.title: PILGRIM OF LIGHT
X.description: You seek grounding in faith and see meaning in trials. For you, self-discovery is inseparable from your relationship with God. Scripture and prayer are your guides, and community is your support on the journey.

I.title: SEEKER OF THE STRAIGHT PATH
I.description: You seek balance between trust in the Almighty and your own effort. Patience, gratitude, and justice aren't just words — they're daily practice. Spiritual reflection is your source of direction.

howToUseList: Look for a specialist or guide who works in an approach close to you
Pay attention to which questions and techniques resonate with you
Use the strengths of your profile in everyday life
Remember: there is no perfect approach — what matters most is trust

recommendations.C: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy may suit you well. It provides concrete tools for working with thoughts and behaviors. You'll be able to set clear goals and track your progress.
recommendations.P: Psychoanalytic therapy may resonate with you. You'll be able to explore the deeper causes of your experiences, understand unconscious scripts, and work with recurring patterns.
recommendations.G: Gestalt therapy will help you develop contact with your body and the present moment. You'll learn to complete unfinished situations, express feelings, and find resources in the here and now.
recommendations.E: Existential therapy offers a space to explore fundamental questions: meaning, freedom, solitude, death. You'll be able to find your own answers.
recommendations.S: You may not need formal therapy right now. You already have your own resources and ways of coping. If you ever want to deepen your self-knowledge — you can always come back.
recommendations.X: Christian spiritual guidance may be your path. A conversation with a priest, spiritual director, or Christian counselor can help you connect self-discovery with faith, and Scripture with daily life.
recommendations.I: Islamic spiritual guidance may be your direction. A conversation with an imam or Muslim counselor can help you find balance between tawakkul and personal effort, and deepen your connection with the Almighty.

footer.disclaimer: This quiz is a self-exploration tool, not a professional diagnosis. It can help you orient yourself, but it does not replace working with a specialist.
footer.helpText: If you're struggling, having suicidal thoughts, or feel like you can't cope — please reach out to a professional. Call 988 (US) or your local crisis line.
